cards.text: God is still talking to Moses, Israel's leader, laying out the plans for the tabernacle and its priests. Now He adds one more piece of furniture. It's an altar, made of acacia wood.

cards.question: This acacia wood altar gets one special job. What is it for?

cards.text: Then God gives the specs: a small square altar, two cubits tall, with horns, covered in pure gold, and gold-covered poles to carry it. Small, shiny and portable, friend, that's basically ME on my gold base.
God tells Moses exactly where it goes: in front of the veil that hangs before the ark of the Testimony and the mercy seat.

cards.question: God says something about that spot in front of the veil, where the incense altar stands. What is it?

answers.text: It's where He will meet with Moses
It's where the priests will eat their portion
It's where the people will bring their gifts

cards.text: Every morning, when he tends the lamps, Aaron, Moses' brother, burns fragrant incense on this altar. Every. Single. Morning. No snooze button for Aaron.

cards.question: Aaron also burns the incense at ___ when he sets up the lamps.
God says the incense on this altar is to burn only during Aaron's lifetime.

cards.text: Then God lays down some rules for this little altar. Every kitchen has rules, friend, and mine has one big one: NOBODY touches my timer.

cards.question: If it's needed, Aaron can offer a burnt offering on the incense altar.

cards.text: Once a year, for all the generations to come, Aaron makes atonement on the horns of this altar. God says, "The altar is most holy to the LORD."

cards.question: What does Aaron use when he makes atonement on the incense altar's horns once a year?

answers.text: The blood of the sin offering
The ashes of the burnt offering

cards.text: Then the LORD switches topics on Moses: a census, a count of the Israelites. When a man is counted, he must pay the LORD a ransom for his life.

cards.question: If each man pays his ransom when he's counted, no ___ will come on them.

cards.text: The ransom is a half shekel, by the sanctuary shekel, from every man twenty or older who's counted. Friend, the last time I had a price on me, it was a 25 cent sticker in a closing-sale bin, and I felt like a BARGAIN.

cards.question: How does the census half shekel work for the rich and the poor?

answers.text: Everyone gives the same half shekel
The rich give double what the poor give
Each man gives what he can afford

cards.question: God says the census money is used for the service of the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses another piece: a bronze basin on a bronze stand, filled with water for washing.

cards.question: Where does God tell Moses to set the bronze basin?

answers.text: Between the Tent of Meeting and the altar
Behind the veil beside the ark
At the far edge of the camp

cards.text: Aaron and his sons wash there whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting or come up to the altar to present an offering. Same rule in my bakery, friend: NOBODY touches the dough until they wash up.

cards.question: Before they serve, Aaron and his sons wash their ___ and ___ in the bronze basin.
God gives a serious reason why the priests must wash at the basin. What is it?

answers.text: So that they will not die
So that the people will trust them
So that the altar will stay clean

cards.text: Next, God gives Moses a recipe with the finest spices: liquid myrrh, cinnamon, fragrant cane and cassia, weighed out by the shekel, plus a hin of olive oil. Friend, you had me at RECIPE.

cards.question: What do all those fine spices and olive oil become?

cards.text: Moses is to anoint with it the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony, the table, the lampstand and the altar of burnt offering with their utensils, the incense altar, and the basin with its stand. Friend, that's a LOT of anointing.

cards.question: God says anything that touches these anointed things becomes unclean.
Besides the Tent of Meeting and its furnishings, who does Moses anoint with this oil?

cards.text: Then God gives Moses a message for the Israelites: this is His sacred anointing oil for the generations to come.

cards.question: An Israelite may make oil with the same formula for his own use.

cards.text: God puts it plainly: "It is holy, and it must be holy to you." Friend, this is the one recipe in all creation a baker does NOT get to copy.

cards.question: What happens to anyone who mixes perfume like the sacred oil or puts it on an outsider?

answers.text: He is cut off from his people
He pays a fine of a half shekel
He washes in the basin seven days

cards.text: Last, God gives Moses a recipe for incense: gum resin, onycha, galbanum and pure frankincense in equal measures, blended by a perfumer and seasoned with salt. Equal measures, friend, no eyeballing it, and believe me, I have eyeballed a LOT of chocolate chips.

cards.question: Some of the incense is ground into fine powder and placed in front of the ___ in the Tent of Meeting.
An Israelite may make this incense at home just to enjoy how it smells.

cards.text: Holy to the LORD, start to finish. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because God's not done giving Moses instructions.

findings.problem: Story card 15 says the half shekel comes 'from every man twenty or older who's counted.' That already tells the baker everyone pays the same amount. It rules out 'The rich give double what the poor give' and 'Each man gives what he can afford' before card 16 asks about the rich and the poor.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This setup line rules out the wrong answers on card 16. 'From every man' plus a fixed half shekel leaves only one answer that fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke calls the anointing oil 'the one recipe in all creation a baker does NOT get to copy.' The passage says the same about the incense formula two cards later (Exodus 30:37-38). The line points out something the text shows is false. It could also nudge the baker toward 'True' on card 17.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'basin' was already ruled out. Stop 2 card 2 taught that the basin sits between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, so a baker knows it isn't 'in the Tent of Meeting' in front of anything.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The list of things to anoint (Exodus 30:26-28) is told item by item. The card names every piece of furniture instead of saying in a few words what the list covers.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: Exodus 30:9 forbids unauthorized incense on this altar. That detail is never told, and later passages build on it. Card 9 only says God 'lays down some rules,' and card 10 asks only about the burnt offering.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card uses context from outside the passage ('still talking to Moses... laying out the plans for the tabernacle and its priests,' from Exodus 25-29) but gives no reference for it. It cites only Exodus 30:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'Aaron, Moses' brother' is a fact from outside the passage (Exodus 4:14). The card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Exodus 30 is made up entirely of building plans (incense altar, basin) and rules for offerings (census ransom, oil and incense formulas). Both are listed as long stretches, which get one summary story card and no choice cards. The walkthrough instead gives the whole passage full stops with many choice cards. The docs don't say what to do when a whole assigned passage is long-stretch material.
findings.question: When an entire passage is building plans or offering rules, should it still get a full walkthrough with choice cards, or does the long-stretch rule apply, and if so, how should Prep fill a passage that is nothing but long stretch?
